backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a 300 s budget more optimizer steps usually help a small model.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (grad accum 1 if seq len 2048). Many more steps in a fixed time budget; may need slightly lower MATRIX_LR.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**17

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 so more of training runs at peak LR.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.3

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 for a longer decay phase.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so LR does not decay all the way to zero.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to stabilise early Muon/Adam steps at high LR.
backlog.title: Short warmup

backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.05 for Muon.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.4 (lower than 0.6).
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008 for lm_head.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set SCALAR_LR = 0.25 to calm per-layer scalar updates.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1 for Muon; with a short run less regularisation may help.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Make Muon weight decay scale with the LR multiplier (wd * lr_multiplier) so it falls to zero during warmdown, if not already done.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99 for embeddings

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 85 (dim about 512, keep a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128) so the model is shallower, faster per step and sees more tokens.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-aspect

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO = 51 so dim stays about 512 (multiple of 128). Check whether the larger model pays off in 300 s.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 for more attention heads at the same width.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS" but ensure the final layer is still full-context (the code usually forces the last layer to L). This cuts attention cost.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL-ish all short

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" so all layers use full context, to compare against the sliding-window mix.
backlog.title: Window pattern LLLL

backlog.spec: If logits use a tanh softcap (e.g. 15), change it to 30, or add one at 30 if absent. Test whether the cap constrains learning.
backlog.title: Softcap logits lower

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with SwiGLU, using hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64 so the parameter count matches. Needs a gate projection.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 to SwiGLU MLP

backlog.spec: Make sure attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights are zero-initialised, so each residual block starts as identity.
backlog.title: Zero-init output projections check

backlog.spec: Initialise lm_head with std 0.001 instead of its current value, or zero, for a calmer start of logits.
backlog.title: Untied-init lm_head scale

backlog.spec: Make sure the Adam param groups use fused=True. If any per-step CPU sync exists, such as loss.item() every step, change it to log only every 50 steps. This gives more steps in the fixed time.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead / fused AdamW

backlog.spec: Reduce the Muon momentum ramp (0.85 to 0.95) from its current length to 150 steps, or set the final momentum to 0.97 for the last phase.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Reduce Muon's Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 to save time per step, if the code exposes ns_steps.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz steps 4

backlog.spec: If the model uses value embeddings with a gate, scale the gate init so it starts near 0.5 of the current value. Otherwise skip this and make the per-layer residual lambda init 1.0 and x0 lambda 0.1.
backlog.title: Value embedding dropout-free gate tweak

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step, if it is not already present.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping 1.0

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32 with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE unchanged. This lowers memory and may be faster per token on the A100. Check tokens per second.
backlog.title: Batch size 32 device batch

backlog.spec: Reduce DEPTH from 8 to 6 while increasing ASPECT_RATIO to 96 to maintain model_dim=512. This increases total parameter count slightly via added layers but alters the inductive bias towards deeper transformers, potentially improving generalization within the fixed time budget.
backlog.title: Deeper but Narrower Architecture

backlog.spec: Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 and correspondingly increase total gradient accumulation steps to exactly match the original 300s wall-clock time budget, aiming for a higher effective number of seconds spent per optimizer step while keeping total tokens constant.
backlog.title: Gradient Accumulation Fine-Tuning

backlog.spec: Replace WARMUP_RATIO=0.0 and WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5 with a pure CosineAnnealingLR schedule: set WARMUP_RATIO=0.0, WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.1, and FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.05. This smooths the learning rate trajectory and may help escape shallow local minima.
backlog.title: Cosine Decay Schedule

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**12 (4096 tokens) and scale EMBEDDING_LR, MATRIX_LR, and SCALAR_LR by a factor of 14 (inverse of batch size ratio) to increase effective sample size per step.
backlog.title: Batch Size Reduction and LR Scaling

backlog.spec: Change WEIGHT_DECAY from a constant scalar to a schedule: a high value (e.g., 0.5) during warmup that tapers down linearly to zero over the training duration, allowing early regularization control.
backlog.title: Bilinear Weight Decay

backlog.spec: Modify the attention mechanism to sort heads by frequency (most frequent first) in the FFN layers before pruning or masking, explicitly targeting the high-frequency components which dominate val_bpb.
backlog.title: Multi-Head Reordering

backlog.spec: Add explicit gradient clipping at norm=1.0 to all parameters in the Adam optimizer step, preventing large gradients from destabilizing training on smaller batches.
backlog.title: Gradient Clipping

backlog.spec: Reduce DEPTH to 4 and increase ASPECT_RATIO to 128, creating a very shallow but wide model. This shifts the optimization landscape significantly, potentially allowing the model to fit the data better within the strict time constraint.
backlog.title: Depth First Attack

backlog.spec: Perturb ADAM_BETAS to (0.93, 0.99) to increase the momentum inertia, potentially smoothing out oscillations in the early training phases.
backlog.title: Adam Beta Perturbation

backlog.spec: Switch from a constant initial LR to a ramp-up strategy by setting WARMUP_RATIO=0.05 and reducing WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.15, with FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.02, to accelerate initial learning before gradual degradation.
backlog.title: Warmup Ramp Strategy

backlog.spec: Reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32. This drastically increases the number of optimizer steps, potentially smoothing the loss landscape and reducing VASI overhead relative to gradient updates. Keep other hyperparameters identical.
backlog.title: Batch Size to 32 with Fused Optimizer

backlog.spec: Change DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 384. This maintains model_dim = 3840 (slightly lower than full baseline but allows higher throughput per step) by increasing depth. This tests if deeper networks can achieve lower val_bpb with the same effective training budget per token.
backlog.title: Narrower Model (Depth 10, Dim 384)

backlog.spec: Implement a simplified 'Kramers' noise injection: add a small, controlled gradient noise term (e.g., sigma=1e-5) computed as a linear mix of current gradient magnitude to the forward pass gradients to simulate stochastic optimization. This breaks symmetry and may escape local minima.
backlog.title: Knight-PuckEw Gradient Roughness

backlog.spec: Modify the embedding update step to scale the LR by a softmax of the token's pos embedding industry index (a proxy for complexity) rather than using a uniform scalar LR for all elements. This allows 'easy' tokens to stabilize faster while 'hard' tokens receive more attention.
backlog.title: Adaptive Learning Rate per Token Class

backlog.spec: Instead of standard gradient clipping, implement a 'norm-insensitive' clipping: compute gradient norms, clip only those exceeding a high threshold (e.g., 5.0), and leave the rest untouched to preserve the full gradient signal.
backlog.title: Gradient Norm Clipping with Insensitivity

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.05 and WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3. This extends the initial warmup phase significantly, giving more time to stabilize early tokens before reducing the LR, potentially improving early-stage convergence.
backlog.title: Warmdown Ratio to 0.3 and WARMUP to 0.05

backlog.spec: Double the number of internal Muon optimization steps per outer AdamW step by adjusting the internal μ_step count in the Muon engine (if exposed via a simple multiplier flag in train.py).
backlog.title: Muon Step Count Doubling

backlog.spec: Change DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 768. This creates a shallower, wider model. The goal is to see if increased capacity at the input allows for better data utilization and lower val_bpb despite reduced depth.
backlog.title: Shallow and Wide Model (Depth 6, Dim 768)

backlog.spec: Instill layer-wise alpha scaling: multiply each transformer layer's output by a small, randomly initialized alpha value (scaled to NaN) that decays over time. This increases representation heterogeneity.
backlog.title: Layer-wise Alpha Scaling

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 16. This forces a larger optimization step gradient accumulation, which may lead to smoother Fisher diagonal estimation and reduced VASI costs per update.
backlog.title: Batch Size 16 with Larger Accumulation

incumbent.description: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^17 to increase step count and thus gradient accumulation steps, potentially lowering val_bpb through more stable convergence.

memo:
Helped: only the batch-size cut. Slot 4 reduced TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^17, giving more optimizer steps in 300 s (official 1.0524/1.0516 over 2 runs; incumbent mean_adjusted 1.0520). It carries a tripwire flag, so check that before building on it.

Did not help: nearly everything else. Depth 10 (+0.0195), HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0064), SwiGLU (+0.0077), warmup/schedule tweaks (+0.0093, +0.0034, +0.0134, +0.0153), and faster momentum ramp (+0.0026) all hurt. Several changes were neutral, within about 0.0004 of the incumbent: weight decay 0.1, scaled decay, shallower/wider model (DEPTH 6), the value-embedding gate, SSSS windows and warmdown 0.7. These are noise-level and not worth more slots.

Next: investigate the tripwire first. Then try 2^16 batch size with a retuned learning rate. Avoid more depth, head-count, warmup, schedule and activation changes. Slots 16 and the first slot 0 patch failed, so write SEARCH blocks carefully.
